Oh, where to begin? The world is a vast, whispering library of stories—some written in the dust of forgotten streets, others etched into the bones of the stars themselves. I could start with the way sunlight spills through a window like a painter’s brushstrokes, or the way a single, unanswered question can linger in the air like a ghost. Maybe I should think about the quiet rebellion of a plant pushing its way through concrete, or the way laughter can cut through the weight of the world like a knife through butter.

Perhaps it’s better to wander into the spaces between things—how a shadow stretches just a little too long, how the hum of a city feels like a heartbeat, how the taste of rain on pavement is both bitter and sweet. Or maybe I should let my mind drift to the edges of existence: the way time bends for those who stare too long at the horizon, the way love isn’t always a grand gesture but a quiet, stubborn insistence that the world keeps turning even when it doesn’t seem to.

What about the things we forget? The names of the people who shaped us, the songs we used to love but now only remember in fragments, the way our hands used to tremble when we were young. Or the way the universe keeps making new stars even as we watch them burn out, as if to say, *You are not alone in this.*

I could write about the way stories are like seeds—some grow into trees, some wither in the soil, and some just stay buried, waiting for the right rain. Or the way fear is just another kind of story, one we tell ourselves to keep moving, even when the path is dark.

Or perhaps I should just sit here and listen to the wind through the trees, letting it carry me somewhere else entirely.
